Let three lessons be read from the Prophecy, three lessons from a Sermon, and three lessons from an Exposition. The first three lessons are from the second seat; the remainder, in order, from the major seat; the ninth is read by the lord archbishop.

The first and second responsories are sung two by two by members of the second seat; the third responsory by three from the second seat in copes. The fourth and fifth responsories are sung two by two by members of the major seat. The sixth responsory is sung by the lord archbishop, together with the dean and cantor, in copes. The seventh and eighth responsories are sung two by two by members of the major seat. The ninth responsory is sung by three from the major seat in copes.

The last three lessons are to be read in copes, and the same arrangement is to be followed on other triple feasts.

Responsory 1: “Today for us” (*Hodie nobis*). Let the entire choir stand while the verse “Glory in the highest” (*Gloria in excelsis*) is sung.

## At Mass on Septuagesima

Responsory—that is, Gradual—“In times of need” (*Adjutor in opportunitatibus*), sung by two from the second seat in the pulpit, in albs. Verse: “For not forever” (*Quoniam non in finem*).

Each of them is to receive one gallon of wine [Note: Now five solidi.] from the cellar of the lord archbishop.

## At Vespers

[Col. 0125A]

178 The following responsory is to be sung at Vespers until Lent, except on Saturdays and on feasts with nine lessons. On Sunday, one from the second seat; on ferial days, one from the first—that is, lowest—seat: “My hope” (*Spes mea*).

## Ash Wednesday
[Note: After Compline, let holy water be sprinkled by the dean or the hebdomadary, and let this be done until the Lord’s Supper, except on Sundays.]

## The First Sunday of Lent, at Mass

Four canons shall sing the Tract, two from the major stall and two from the second stall, in white garments before the altar: “He who dwells.” Let them sing their verses two and two; let all begin together and all end together: “With length of days”; and thus it shall be concluded.  
[Note: Now in copes.]

## Monday within the First Week of Lent

Let this prescribed order, together with the kissing of the stalls by each person, be observed from the beginning of the fast on this Monday, for the Hours, antiphons, and chapters, until the Passion; and let the kissing of the stalls continue until the Vespers of the Lord’s Supper.

## Ember Saturday

At this Mass, in the prayer before the Epistle, “Let us bend the knee” shall not be said, out of reverence for Saint Paul. The first four lessons shall be read from the major stall, and the fifth lesson from the second stall: “The angel of the Lord.” Four responsories shall be sung from the first stall, in white garments before the eagle; and the Tract “Praise the Lord” by two from the major stall, in white garments [Note: Now in copes.] before the altar. At the first five prayers, “The Lord be with you” shall not be said, but “Let us pray.”

## The Second Sunday of Lent, at Mass

Two boys shall begin “From my needs” at the pulpit, and the choir shall finish this verse. Two boys shall sing only the second verse, “To you, O Lord,” and the choir shall finish the verse. Two boys shall begin “For indeed all,” and the choir shall conclude it. Another Tract shall follow. Four canons—two from the major stall and two from the second stall—shall sing the Tract “I will bless the Lord” before the altar in white garments [Note: In copes.].

## Palm Sunday, at Mass

Two from the second stall shall sing the Responsory in white garments: “You have held the hand”; Verse: “How good,” not to be repeated. Each shall receive one gallon of wine [Note: Now five solidi.] from the cellarer of the lord archbishop.

The Tract shall be sung before the altar by four canons—two from the major stall and two from the second stall—in white garments [Note: In copes]: “My God, my God, look.”

## On the Ascension of the Lord

The Invitatory shall be sung by four of the senior canons, who shall direct the choir throughout Matins; two senior or older canons shall direct the nocturns, and the other two shall direct Lauds.

## On the Feast of Pentecost, at First Vespers

Psalm: “My soul magnifies the Lord.” Meanwhile, the major altar shall be incensed by the lord archbishop, if he is present; afterward he shall return to his cathedral chair. The tombs of the kings and the altar of blessed Mary shall be incensed by two priest-canons. On their return, those same canons shall incense the lord archbishop and the lord dean; afterward the choir shall be incensed by two boys. Let this be done on all triple feasts, provided that the archbishop has celebrated the service. Three from the second stall shall sing: “Let us bless the Lord.”

### At Matins

Let three lessons from the Exposition be read: “If anyone loves me,” and let them be in copes of different colors. Candlesticks and a thurible shall be used at the first lesson. All the responsories shall be sung in copes: the first responsory by three from the second stall, the second responsory by three from the third stall, and the third responsory [Note: Now four cantors.] by three of the senior canons.

### At Mass

If the archbishop is present, he shall have with him seven deacons and the same number of subdeacons, of whom twelve shall be from the second stall. Those twelve ought to dine with the lord archbishop, or each shall receive two solidi [Note: Now five solidi.] from the purse of the said lord.

“Christ conquers” shall be sung by two canons, and each ought to receive five solidi from the purse of the lord archbishop, which he himself must hand to the said canons with his own hand. [Note: They shall dine with the lord archbishop, together with the deacon, subdeacon, and five singers.] Otherwise, the presbyter senior in rank shall perform the office.

## On the Feast of the Holy Trinity, at Mass

When the Gospel has been finished, “I believe in one God” shall be said. Meanwhile, the text [Note: That is, the Gospel book.] shall be carried by the subdeacon to the dean, with the thurible carried before him by the deacon.

If the dean is absent, the subdeacon shall carry it through the choir to be kissed, while a boy incenses it. Let this likewise be done on all feasts at which “I believe in one God” is said.

## On the Feast of Corpus Christi, at Matins

The first three lessons shall be read from the second stall; the remaining lessons from the major stall. The archbishop shall read the ninth lesson from his chair, if he is present.

## On the Feast of the Purification, at Mass

Each person shall hold a burning candle, which he shall offer after the Gospel.

## On the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary, at Matins

“Te Deum laudamus” shall be begun festively, and the altar shall be incensed by the priest. Two boys shall stand before the altar holding two candlesticks. Let this be done on all triple feasts.

## On the Commemoration of All the Departed, at Vespers

Psalm: “My soul magnifies the Lord.” Let only the major altar and the celebrant be incensed.

## Throughout the Year, Every Day, at Compline

If the dean is present, “I confess” shall be said to the dean by both choirs.

## The Order of the Office of Matins

On Sundays until Easter, two from the second stall shall sing the Invitatory. The antiphons of the nocturns shall be sung from the major stall, and in each nocturn the last antiphon shall end with a neume. The first three lessons shall be read from the first stall; the fourth and fifth lessons from the second stall; the remaining lessons from the major stall. The responsories shall be performed in the same order. This order shall be observed on Sundays.

### At Lauds

The five antiphons of Lauds shall be begun from the second stall, and the last shall end with a neume, on all Sundays. “Let us bless the Lord”: one boy from the side of the hebdomadary [shall sing it] throughout the year.

### At the Canonical Hours

Note that all the antiphons of the Hours, including on Sundays and feast days, shall be begun from the second stall and shall end with a neume.

### At Vespers

All the antiphons shall be begun from the second stall and shall end with a neume on all Sundays.

## On Weekdays Throughout the Year

One from the second stall shall sing the Invitatory. The antiphons of the nocturn shall be sung from the first stall, with the last ending in a neume. On all weekdays, the first responsory shall be sung from the first stall, the second responsory from the second stall, and the third responsory from the major stall.

On all weekdays, the antiphons of Lauds shall be sung from the first stall.

All the weekday antiphons and those of three-lesson feasts—at Nocturns, Lauds, the Hours, Vespers, and Compline—shall be sung from the first stall, except the antiphons “Benedictus” and “Magnificat” [addition: “Nunc dimittis”], which shall be begun from the major stall and end with a neume; also except the last antiphon of Nocturns and the last of Lauds, and all the antiphons of the Hours, which shall have a neume, with the sole exception of the antiphon “God, hear,” which is without a neume [Note: Now it is said with a neume.]. At Compline, the first of the two shall end with a neume and the last without one.

## On Saturdays

On Saturdays until the Advent of the Lord, the service of Saint Mary shall be performed, unless a nine-lesson feast, a solemn octave, or an Ember Day falls on one of these days. It shall not be omitted on account of three-lesson feasts. Friday Vespers shall be of blessed Mary, as follows: Antiphon, “Glorious Mother”; Psalm, “I will give thanks”; and the remaining psalms of the day, etc.

### At Matins

The ninth responsory shall be sung by two from the major stall, in surplices.

# The Blessing of the Chrism on Maundy Thursday

*(From the manuscript Ordinaries of the cathedral church of Rouen and of the Bigot Library.)*

Twelve suburban presbyters, together with the Christianitatis dean, shall be prepared with the archbishop in all priestly vestments. By them the chrism and oil shall be consecrated with the archbishop. On this day a larger number of hosts shall be consecrated, so that Communion may be received on the following day; and any hosts that remain shall be honorably reserved after Mass.

After the Sanctus, twelve city presbyters, vested in all priestly garments, together with the Christianitatis dean, shall go through the door on the left side of the choir to the chapel of Saint John for the oil of the sick, and shall return to the choir through the great door. When it has been consecrated, it shall be carried back to its proper place.

“Therefore, most merciful Father” shall be said as far as “through whom you create all these things, O Lord, always good things.” At this point the twelve presbyters, with six deacons and six subdeacons [Note: These things are not observed in the Church of Rouen], and six clerics from the first stall—two of whom shall carry two crosses, two others two thuribles, and the remaining two two candlesticks between the two crosses—shall proceed.

Several vested presbyters shall carry the chrism oil, and other presbyters shall carry the oil of catechumens between the two thuribles. Thus, with the procession properly arranged, they shall leave through the left door of the choir, go to the chapel of Saint John, and return before the major altar through the middle of the choir.

A pall shall be placed over the procession and carried by four presbyters. Two vested deacons [in white copes] shall sing before the procession the verses “O Redeemer, receive this song”; those following, wearing stoles, shall respond: “O Redeemer.”

While the consecration of the Lord’s body and blood is taking place, the Christianitatis dean [Note: That is, the dean of the city’s parish priests.] shall hold the ampulla of the oil of the sick before the altar and present it to the archbishop. The archbishop, together with the twelve presbyters, shall say, so that they may be heard by them: “I exorcise you.” Then follows: “Send forth, O Lord, the Paraclete Spirit from heaven.”

After the Lord’s Prayer has been completed, the archbishop, together with the twelve presbyters, shall ascend the episcopal chair behind the altar. The twelve presbyters, the crosses, candlesticks, and thuribles shall then be arranged around him.

When this has been completed, the archbishop shall turn toward the east and begin the consecration of the principal chrism. First, he shall mix balsam with the oil; then he shall breathe upon it three times and say: “I exorcise you, creature of oil.” Then, in a loud voice: “Throughout all ages of ages. Amen.” Preface: “Who in the beginning, among other things…”

When this has been completed, the archbishop shall greet the uncovered chrism in this manner: “Hail, holy chrism,” three times. The other priests shall greet it in the same way.

When this has been completed, the oil shall be blessed: “I exorcise you, creature of oil.” Another prayer: “God of increase.”

When this has been completed, the archbishop shall greet the uncovered oil in this manner: “Hail, holy oil,” three times. The other priests shall likewise greet it in this way.

When this has been completed, the chrism and holy oil shall be carried back to the place where they are to be divided. As they return, the deacons shall sing as on the outward journey, in an orderly procession as before, while the others respond: “O Redeemer.”

When this has been completed, the archbishop shall wash his hands and say: “Throughout all ages of ages. Amen. May the peace of the Lord be always with you,” etc.

# The Following Are Some Matters Worth Noting

*Excerpted from the same manuscript Ordinary for the use of the cathedral church of Rouen.*

*(From the same Bigot manuscript.)*

# The Mandatum, or Washing of the Feet

## Maundy Thursday

After the meal, the Mandatum of the poor shall be performed, and the Mandatum of the clerics shall be celebrated as follows.

The lord archbishop, vested in an alb with the deacon and subdeacon and candle-bearers, shall go to the nave of the church and perform the Mandatum after the example of the Lord. As many of the senior clergy as he wishes, in albs, shall wash the feet of the others.

The lord archbishop must arrange for each canon present and for the keeper of the vestments to receive one cloth (in French, *devantel*), one basin (in French, *gatte*), one earthen pot, and one willow cup. Each canon shall have one cleric from the said [alternative: first] stall, in a surplice, to draw [alternative: take] wine and water for him for the poor.

Meanwhile, with the cantor beginning “The Lord Jesus, a new commandment,” the following shall be sung:

- Psalm: “Blessed are the undefiled.”
- Antiphon: “If I, the Lord.”
- Psalm: “Blessed are those who search.”
- Antiphon: “After the Lord had risen.”
- “May God have mercy,” and “You call me.”
- Verse: “For I have given you an example.”
- Antiphon: “By this they shall know.”
- Antiphon: “In those days.”
- Psalm: “Have mercy.”
- Verse: “Her sins are forgiven.”
- Antiphon: “Then Mary anointed his feet.”
- “You have blessed.”
- Antiphon: “Let us love one another.”
- Verse: “And this commandment.”
- Antiphon: “When brothers dwell together.”
- Verse: “Where there is charity.”
- Psalm: “Have mercy on me.”
- Antiphon: “Lord, do you wash my feet?”
- “He came to Simon.”
- Antiphon: “Lord, not my feet only.”
- Verse: “What I am doing, you will understand.”

When this has been completed, they shall go to the chapter house [manuscript: chapter]. There the deacon, vested in an alb and stole, with candles and a thurible, shall read, in the manner of a lesson, “Before the feast day.” Other deacons or priests shall read and assist him until they come to “Rise, let us go from here.”

Then wafers shall be distributed with wine. When this has been completed [alternative: done], they shall return to the choir and say Compline in silence as follows.

# Good Friday

When None has been completed, they shall go to bless the fire, proceeding in verse and in silence: “Have mercy on me, O God,” as on Thursday. After it has been blessed, they shall return to the choir, proceeding in verse with Psalm “The Lord is my light.”

When this has been completed, the lord archbishop—or a priest—vested in all the priestly garments, together with the deacon and subdeacon in white garments, shall approach the altar, and the service shall begin as follows.

A lesson shall be read without a title at the eagle. One canon from the second stall shall read “In distress.” Two from the second stall, in white garments before the eagle, shall sing the Tract “Lord, I have heard.” Then shall follow “The Lord be with you,” “Let us pray,” “Let us bend the knee,” “Arise,” and “God, from whom Judas…”

“Throughout all ages of ages,” and, when “Amen” has been said, the subdeacon in white shall read, without a title and in the manner of a lesson before the eagle, “The Lord spoke to Moses.”

Four canons—two from the major stall and two from the second—shall sing their verses two and two, and, in white garments before the altar, shall sing the Tract “Deliver me, O Lord.”

The deacon, in an alb [with maniple and stole], shall read the Passion before the altar in the manner of a lesson, except for the voice of the Lord, which shall be read in the manner of the Gospel. “The Lord be with you” shall not be said, nor shall the response “Glory to you, O Lord” be given. It shall begin as follows:

“The Passion of our Lord Jesus Christ according to John. Jesus went out,” etc.

When they have come to the place where it says, “They divided my garments,” two clerics shall strip the altar of the cloths that had previously been placed upon it. The altar signifies the Lord; the cloths signify the apostles, who, when Jesus had been seized, all fled [alternative: abandoned him].

When they have come to the place where it says, “And, bowing his head, he gave up the spirit,” all shall prostrate themselves on the ground.

When the Passion has been completed, the solemn prayers shall be said without interruption. The chasuble shall not be removed, and the knees shall not be bent for the Jews.

At the first prayer, “Let us bend the knee,” “Arise,” and “Through the Lord” shall not be said. At the second prayer, “Let us bend the knee,” “Arise,” and “Through the Lord” shall be said.

They begin as follows:

“Let us pray. Beloved, let us pray for the Church.”

“Let us pray. Almighty and eternal God, who reveals your glory…”

“Let us pray also for our most blessed pope.”

“Let us bend the knee.”

“Almighty and eternal God, in whose hand…”

“Through…”

“Let us pray also for our catechumens, that God and our Lord…”

“Let us bend the knee.”

“Almighty and eternal God, consolation of the sorrowful…”

“Through…”

“Let us pray also for the heretics.”

“Let us bend the knee. Arise.”

“Almighty and eternal God, who saves all…”

“Through…”

“Let us pray also for the faithless Jews.”

Here “Let us bend the knee” shall not be said.

“Almighty and eternal God, who also [regards] the Jewish people…”

“Through…”

“Let us pray also for the pagans, that almighty God may remove…”

“Let us bend the knee. Arise.”

“Almighty and eternal God, who does not desire death…”

When these things have been completed, the lord archbishop or priest shall remove the chasuble and proceed with the deacon and subdeacon. While they sit barefoot on the choir step, two priests vested in black chasubles shall hold the veiled cross behind the altar and say in a supplicating voice: “My people.”

Two deacons, barefoot before the eagle and vested in black copes, shall respond, bending their knees: “Agios o Theos”—“Holy God.”

The lord archbishop and the others, as before: “Holy God.”

Then two presbyters shall hold the cross before the altar and say: “What more ought I to have done?” The deacons, as before: “Agios o Theos”—“Holy God.” The lord archbishop and the others, as before: “Holy God.”

When this has been completed, the lord archbishop or priest shall uncover the cross with the staff, kneeling, and say: “Behold the wood of the cross.” The choir shall prostrate itself on the ground and complete the antiphon.

Psalm: “Blessed are the undefiled.”

The choir shall repeat the antiphon “Behold the wood.”

The cross shall then first be adored by the lord archbishop, and afterward by the others in order.

The adoration of all shall be performed so that each person’s belly remains on the ground [Note: Thus in John of Avranches, p. 60, although it is somewhat differently stated in Augustine.]. For while one kneels, according to Augustine on Psalm 43, there still remains something to be humbled. But when someone humbles himself so that his whole body remains on the ground, nothing further remains in him of humility.

The offering made for the adoration of the cross shall be distributed in equal portions to the two who sang “My people” and to the two who sang “Agios.”

While the cross is adored, the cantor shall begin the antiphon “We adore your cross.”

Psalm: “May God have mercy.”

Another antiphon: “Your cross.”

Another antiphon: “Let us adore the sign of the cross.”

“While the Maker…”

Another antiphon: “O wondrous price.”

The hymn “Faithful Cross” shall be sung.

“Sing, my tongue…”

“Faithful Cross.”

If necessary, the hymn “Six hours” shall also be sung.

When these things have been completed and the cross has been adored by clergy and people, the crucifix, in remembrance of the blood and water flowing from the Redeemer’s side, shall be washed with wine and water [Note: Today the cross is neither carried to the sepulchre nor washed. Alternative: absent.]. While it is being washed, it shall be lifted up high, and the antiphon “Above all the trees” shall be sung.

When the antiphon has been completed, the lord archbishop or priest, together with the two presbyters who sang “My people,” shall carry the crucifix to the sepulchre. The cantor shall begin [manuscript of the cathedral: When this has been completed, the crucifix shall be carried to the sepulchre by the two presbyters who sang] the Responsory “Like a sheep led to the slaughter,” with its verse and return.

When it has been placed there, the antiphon “In peace I will lie down and sleep” shall be said.

Afterward the archbishop or priest shall wash the door of the sepulchre and begin in a subdued voice the Responsory “The Lord has been buried.”

When these things have been completed, the lord archbishop or priest shall put on a black chasuble. After washing his hands, he shall proceed with great reverence to the sacristy, preceded by thuribles, candlesticks, and torches. He shall bring the Lord’s body, reserved since the previous day, to the altar, and wine and water shall be placed in the chalice, as is customary on other days.

First, before the altar, he shall make confession [Note: Today confession is not made.], saying “I confess,” etc. Having done this, he shall approach the altar, pause briefly, and say in a subdued voice [Note: No mention is made here of elevating the host]:

“Let us pray: At the command of salvation…”  
“Our Father.”  
The choir shall respond: “But deliver us from evil.”

The lord archbishop or priest shall say “Amen” quietly and privately.

“Deliver us, we beseech you, O Lord.”

At “Through the same Lord” he shall perform the fraction. Having done this, he shall sing in a subdued voice: “Throughout all ages of ages. Amen.” The choir shall respond in the same voice: “Amen.”

“The peace of the Lord” shall not be said, nor shall the “Lamb of God” be sung. Instead, a portion of Christ’s body shall be placed in the chalice, as is customary, and the priest shall say the prayers “Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God” and “Lord Jesus Christ.”

Meanwhile, the priest shall receive the Lord’s body, saying: “The body of our Lord,” etc. Likewise, when he takes the chalice, he shall say: “The body and blood of the Lord,” etc., according to the usual practice.

Those who wish shall receive Communion, as on the preceding day, and a portion of the body of Christ the Lord shall be reserved for viaticum.

Afterward, the lord archbishop or priest, holding the chalice in his hands, shall begin at Vespers in a moderate voice: “The chalice,” etc., as noted yesterday. The choir shall sing Vespers softly.

When the five psalms and the antiphon have been completed, the lord archbishop or priest shall begin the antiphon “When he had received the vinegar.”

Psalm: “My soul magnifies the Lord.”

When this has been completed, the lord archbishop or priest shall wash his hands and, in a moderate voice, without “The Lord be with you,” sing: “Let us pray. Refreshed by life-giving things,” and “Throughout all ages of ages.”

At the end, only “Amen” shall be answered. Thus they shall proceed to the meal of bread and water.

After the meal, the candle-column shall be erected. When this has been completed, Compline shall be said in silence.

# The Public Expulsion of Penitents

## Ash Wednesday

*(From the same Bigot manuscript.)*

At None, the hymn, antiphon, chapter, responsory, and verse shall be taken from the series of psalms [lacuna].

Then the archbishop, or the person who shall be acting in his place, shall prepare himself with the cantor to perform the absolution. The deacon and subdeacon shall be vested in white, and they shall go before the crucifix. There the lord archbishop shall preach a sermon to the people. When it has been completed, all shall prostrate themselves.

The cantor shall begin the seven penitential psalms: “O Lord, rebuke me not in your fury,” etc. When these have been completed, the lord archbishop shall say the appropriate prayers there. The final prayer shall be “Absolution and remission,” etc.

Then the lord archbishop shall proceed to the major altar and bless the ashes upon it, with the appropriate prayers. When these have been completed, the lord archbishop and the other priests shall distribute them, while the following antiphon is sung: “Let us change our clothing.”

Another antiphon: “Between the vestibule and the altar” [alternative: “Near the vestibule and the altar”].

When it has been completed, the lord archbishop shall proceed with the procession to the western doors of the church to expel the penitents, and the cantor shall begin “Hear us, O Lord.”

Psalm: “Save me, O God.”

“ Hear us” shall be repeated.

When these things have been completed, the deacon shall read this sermon: “The voice of blood.” Then the penitents shall be expelled, while “Do not remember” is sung.

The lord archbishop shall then speak with them, and the doors of the church shall be closed [alternative: he shall close them].

When this has been completed, the procession shall return to the altar of the right-hand cross in the chapel of the Holy Spirit, with the cantor beginning this Responsory: “Behold Adam.”

Verse: “Cherubim” [Note: Now the verse “And he made…” is said.]

There, with prostration, prayers shall be said together with “Have mercy on me, O God” and the appropriate prayers.

When this has been completed, two from the second stall shall begin the litany, which they shall conclude in the choir with the procession.

When this has been completed, Mass shall begin and shall be celebrated according to the weekday rite.

# The Reconciliation of Penitents

## Maundy Thursday

*(From the same Bigot manuscript.)*

When None has been completed, the lord archbishop—or his vicar—vested in an alb and stole with a red cope, or a priest without a cope, together with the deacon and subdeacon vested in white and stole, and with the cantor, shall proceed in an orderly procession to the western doors of the church to reconcile the penitents.

The lord archbishop shall sit beside the doors of the church while the procession stands in the nave of the church [Note: We have extracted this reading below from an ancient manuscript in the cathedral library of the church of Rouen.]. The deacon shall read, in the manner of a lesson, this reading: “The time is at hand, O venerable pontiff.”

When the reading has been completed, the lord archbishop or his vicar shall rise and sing the antiphon “Come,” three times, and conclude it.

The cantor shall begin the psalm “I will bless the Lord.” The entire psalm shall be said if necessary, and at each verse the antiphon “Come, come” shall be repeated.

Meanwhile, the lord archbishop or his vicar shall admit the penitents into the church with his staff. The reconciled shall carry burning candles to the altar; the others shall carry extinguished candles or none. The lord archbishop or his vicar shall place his hand upon the heads of those reconciled, giving each the kiss of peace and saying: “Peace be with you.”

When these things have been completed, the procession shall return in silence, and a sermon shall be delivered to the people.

When it has been completed, the lord archbishop, with the deacon and subdeacon, shall say the seven penitential psalms with prostration, the choir responding.

When these have been completed, the antiphon “Do not remember” shall be said. When it has been completed, the lord archbishop shall absolve the prostrate penitents, saying the prayers:

“Kyrie eleison. Christe eleison. Kyrie eleison.”  
“Our Father.”  
“And lead us not…”  
Verse: “Save your servants.”  
Verse: “Send them help.”  
Verse: “O Lord, hear.”  
“The Lord be with you.”

Prayer: “Grant, we beseech you, O Lord, to these your servants…”

Prayer: “Absolution and remission.”

# Sermon of the Archdeacon

## To the Archbishop of Rouen, for the Reconciliation of Public Penitents on Maundy Thursday

*(From a 700-year-old manuscript Pontifical in the cathedral library of Rouen.)*

The time is at hand, O venerable pontiff: a time of vows for the afflicted, suitable for penitents, desirable for those in distress.

Your sons are present, Father—those whom the true mother Church bore in joy to the Lord through the Holy Spirit, but whom, after the devil’s renewed persuasion, she daily mourns as corrupted from their integrity, made wretched, and exiled amid fresh sorrows.

All those who have remained happily in her bosom, and who, under the protection of divine clemency, have remained steadfast in the faith, offer humble prayers for them.

We must remember how that younger son was received by the most merciful father—the son who for so long fed pigs and unhappily squandered the precious resources of his father’s inheritance.

The Father stands open; today there stands open that fountain of David flowing from the Savior’s side, in which menstrual uncleanness is washed away, and in which those soiled by the blackness of sins are whitened like snow through humble confession.

For this purpose God and our Lord appointed you mediator: so that, like that father, you might take the sinner whom you have received and carry him back on your shoulders.

You have received from the Lord the ring of discernment and honor, so that you may mark what must be marked, reveal what must be opened, bind what must be bound, loose what must be loosed, and open the gates of the heavenly kingdom both to believers through the faith of baptism and to the fallen and penitent through the ministry of reconciliation.

May the very tears of these wretched people move your compassion.

Mary wept and was received. On this night the apostle denied him, and, baptized again by his tears, was restored. The tax collector from the customs booth merited apostleship. The robber entered paradise from the cross.

Our mother Jerusalem weeps, praying for her sons, and her tears are upon her cheeks (Lamentations 1:2).

Have mercy, have mercy, Father, because the time has come to have mercy on her (Psalm 101:14).

# Fragments

*From the manuscript Ordinary of the cathedral church of Rouen. The following ceremonies are not observed in that church.*

## At the Nativity of the Lord, at the End of the First Nocturn

All those from the second stall, in surplices and arranged in the form of a crown, shall sing the sequence. The cantor, standing before the choir step in his black cope, shall begin “Blessed Mary.”

## After the Ninth Responsory

All those from the major stall, in surplices, except the dean, shall sing the sequence in the form of a crown. It shall be begun by the cantor: “Whom heaven and earth…”

## On the Paschal Anniversary

The office of the paschal anniversary cannot be performed unless it falls after the octave of Easter.

The order on the paschal anniversary is a feast with a double third responsory. At Vespers, the antiphons shall be sung from the major stall and with a neume.

Antiphon: “Alleluia.”  
Psalms of the day.

The remainder of the office generally agrees with the office of the Sunday in White.

## On the Feast of the Holy Trinity

Note that at the second, fifth, and eighth lessons the major altar and the tombs of the kings shall be incensed, as shall the archbishop and dean, if they are present, by two priest-canons in copes; afterward the choir shall be incensed by two boys. Let this likewise be done on all triple feasts.

## On the Feast of Corpus Christi, at First Vespers

“Magnificat” shall be sung in the sixth and fifth tones.

## On the Purification of Blessed Mary, at First Vespers

A commemoration of Saint Severus shall be made out of reverence for his body, which rests in the church of Rouen.

### At Mass

Mass shall follow; nine copes shall be in the choir.

## On the Days of Easter, Pentecost, the Assumption, the Dedication of the Church, and Saint Romanus, at Mass

All the copes shall be in the choir; nine shall be in a line [alternative: in the middle].

## On the Assumption of Blessed Mary, at First Vespers

The antiphon “Christ has ascended” shall be sung with three repetitions. It shall be sung by the right choir as far as “And this is she”; afterward by the left choir as far as “In which glorious”; then by the right choir as far as “To which devout”; and it shall be concluded by the left choir.

Psalm: “My soul magnifies the Lord,” sung in the sixth and fifth tones.

After the final verse, the antiphon “He has ascended” shall be begun by the left choir and divided into four parts, as noted above. After “Glory to the Father,” it shall be sung by the entire choir together. When “Magnificat” is begun, the major altar shall be incensed.

# The Office of the Children

## On the Feast of Saint John the Evangelist, After Second Vespers

*(From the Bigot manuscript Ordinary.)*
[Col. 0135B] When this has been completed, two boys dressed in tunics and amices, holding candlesticks with burning candles, and all the church boys^203 in copes holding burning candles, shall leave the vestry two by two with their bishop, singing the response “One hundred forty”; in an orderly procession they shall come through the choir and go to the Altar of the Innocents, where they shall make a station, and it shall end there. Three boys shall sing the verse: “These are they who have been bought.” When this has been completed, the antiphon “The Innocents” shall follow. Three boys: “Rejoice.” The bishop: “Let us pray. O God, whose day this is.” On the return, an antiphon or responsory concerning Saint Mary, at pleasure; two boys shall sing the verse “After childbirth”; the bishop: “Let us pray. O God, who are the salvation.” The boys shall say “Let us bless.” The bishop’s blessing shall follow, and one boy shall say in a loud voice, “Bow yourselves for the blessing,” while the others shall answer, “Thanks be to God.” Blessing: “May the almighty Lord bless you,” etc.

On the following day there is a double feast, [Note: [Col. 0135C] The manuscript of the cathedral church adds:] but the boys, by their own choice, make it triple. The bishop shall give the invitatory, with two boys: “Come, let us adore”; psalm, “Come,” etc. The bishop shall read the ninth lesson, “The Angel of the Lord appeared.” While the ninth lesson is being read, the boys shall proceed to the vestry; when it is finished, they shall come out two by two with burning candles, singing the responsory “One hundred forty.” Three boys shall sing the verse and prose, and finish it before the altar in the form of a crown. When this has been completed,^204 the psalm “We praise you, O God” shall be begun; when it is finished, the morning Lauds shall begin there, and they shall return to the choir, where Matins shall be concluded in the middle of the choir.

Antiphon at Lauds: “Herod was angry”; psalm, “The Lord reigns.” Antiphon: “From two years old and under”; psalm, “Shout joyfully.” Antiphon: “A voice in Ramah”; psalm, “O God, God.” Antiphon: “Beneath the throne”; psalm, “Bless.” Three boys shall begin the antiphon “Let the boys render praises” at the pulpit; psalm, “Praise the Lord.” Antiphon: “Let them render praises.” Verse: “Praise him.” Antiphon: “Let them render praises.” Thus the choir shall finish the psalm; at each verse the boys shall say, “Let them render praises,” etc. “Let us bless” at the boys’ pleasure.

A procession shall follow to the Altar of the Innocents, singing the responsory “Worthy from the worthy,” with its verse, and return. The verses shall be at pleasure. Prayer: “O God, who, although …” On the return, an antiphon or responsory concerning Saint Mary, at pleasure, as noted above: “After childbirth.” Let us pray: “O God, who are the salvation,” etc. When this has been completed, the boys with their bishop shall go before the high altar, singing as noted above on the day of Saint Stephen. After the first blessing, the bishop’s blessing shall be as above . . . . . . If it is Sunday, the blessing of water shall follow; after Terce they shall be sprinkled, and then the procession shall follow. It shall be from the Nativity according to its order, and the boys shall be in copes in the upper part, as noted above on the day of Saint Stephen.^205

At Mass. The Introit. All the boys in copes shall govern the choir in the middle of the choir; the bishop shall begin “From the mouths of infants.” Psalm: “O Lord, our Lord.” Kyrie eleison and Gloria festively. Prayer: “O God, whose day this is.” The Epistle shall be sung with the prose, as above, “I saw above the mountain.” Gradual, by the boys, as noted above: “Our soul.” Verse: “The snare.” The bishop, with all the boys, in the form of a crown: “Alleluia, These are they who …” The bishop shall begin the Sequence, “High things, boys.” The Gospel shall be sung: “The Angel of the Lord appeared.” Creed. Offertory: “Our soul,” begun by the bishop, etc. Everything as above. Then let all who wish make offerings, as noted above.

At Vespers, two from the first seat shall govern the choir; the antiphons shall be begun from the first seat and ended with a neume. Antiphon: “With you is princely rule”; psalm, “The Lord said,” etc. Chapter: “These are they who have been bought.” The bishop, with two boys in tunics: responsory “The righteous shall live forever” . . . . . . Antiphon: “O how glorious”; psalm, “My soul magnifies the Lord.” Let “He has cast down the mighty” be sung until the staff is taken up by whoever wishes to take it; Vespers shall be concluded by the dietary, etc.

[Col. 0135]

## OFFICE OF THE STAR, OR OF THE THREE KINGS

(From the manuscript ordinal and book of offices of the Bigot Library.)

[Col. 0135D] ^206 The office of the Three Kings according to the use of the church of Rouen. On the day of Epiphany, after Terce has been sung, three men from the principal seat, dressed in the manner of kings [al. adorned with copes and crowns], and required to be entered in the register, shall come together from three sides before the altar, with their servants carrying the kings’ offerings, dressed in tunics and [Col. 0136D] amices. These servants are to be entered in the register from the secondary seat, at the discretion of the registrar.

Of the three kings, the one in the middle, coming from the east [al. the first standing behind the altar, as though coming from the east], pointing out the star with his staff, shall say loudly: [Note: [Col. 0137] Double-click on the ornament icon that follows to view in full the musical notation whose contents are keyed below.]

[Col. 0137A] “A star shines with extraordinary brilliance.”

The second king, from the right side [al. adding “coming”], shall answer: [Note: [Col. 0137] Double-click on the ornament icon that follows to view in full the musical notation whose contents are keyed below.]

“It reveals that the King of kings has been born.”

The third king, from the left side [al. adding “coming”], shall say: [Note: [Col. 0137] Double-click on the ornament icon that follows to view in full the musical notation whose contents are keyed below.]

“The prophecies had once foretold the one who was to come.”

Then the magi shall kiss one another before the altar and sing together: [Note: [Col. 0137] Double-click on the ornament icon that follows to view in full the musical notation whose contents are keyed below.]

^207

[Col. 0137B] “Let us go, therefore, and seek him, offering him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.”

When this has been completed, the cantor shall begin the responsory: [Note: [Col. 0137] Double-click on the ornament icon that follows to view in full the musical notation whose contents are keyed below.]

“Wise men are coming,” etc.

And the procession shall move. Another responsory shall follow, if necessary. [Note: [Col. 0137] Double-click on the ornament icon that follows to view in full the musical notation whose contents are keyed below.]

[Col. 0137C] “He questioned the magi,” etc.

When the procession has been established in the nave of the church [al. “Procession”], let them make a station [al. “let it make a station”]. When the procession begins to enter the nave of the church, the crown hanging before the altar of the cross [al. “before the cross”], in the manner of a star [al. adding “shall be lit”], and the magi, pointing out the star [al. adding “with their staffs”], shall proceed toward the image of Saint Mary previously placed above the altar of the cross, singing:

“Behold, the star formerly seen in the east again goes before us, shining. This star, I say, reveals the one who has been born, concerning whom Balaam had sung,” [Col. 0137D] saying: “A star shall rise out of Jacob, and a man shall arise from Israel, and he shall crush all the leaders of foreign nations, and the whole earth shall be his possession.”^208

[Col. 0138A] When this has been completed, two men from the principal seat, dressed in dalmatics [al. “dressed in dalmatics”], standing on either side of the altar, shall answer softly [al. “shall say to one another in a subdued voice”]: [Note: [Col. 0138] Double-click on the ornament icon that follows to view in full the musical notation whose contents are keyed below.]

“Who are these men who, guided by the star, approach us bringing unheard-of things?”

The magi shall answer: [Note: [Col. 0138] Double-click on the ornament icon that follows to view in full the musical notation whose contents are keyed below.]

“We are those whom you see: the kings of Tarshish, [Col. 0138B] Arabia, and Sheba, bringing gifts to Christ, the newborn King and Lord, whom we have come to adore, with the star leading us.”^209

Then the two men in dalmatics, opening the curtain, shall say: [Note: [Col. 0138] Double-click on the ornament icon that follows to view in full the musical notation whose contents are keyed below.]

“Behold the child whom you seek; hasten now to adore him, for he himself is the redemption of the world.”

Then the kings, falling together to the ground, shall greet the child, saying: “Hail, Prince of the ages” [Note: [Col. 0137D] This verse with its chant is absent from the manuscript book of offices]. Then one of them shall receive gold from his servant, say, and offer it:

“Receive gold, O King.” [Note: [Col. 0138] Double-click on the ornament icon that follows to view in full the musical notation whose contents are keyed below.]

The second king shall say and offer in this manner:

“Take frankincense; you are truly God.” [Note: [Col. 0138] Double-click on the ornament icon that follows to view in full the musical notation whose contents are keyed below.]

The third shall say and offer:

“Myrrh, the sign of burial.” [Note: [Col. 0138] Double-click on the ornament icon that follows to view in full the musical notation whose contents are keyed below.]

Meanwhile offerings shall be made by the clergy and people [Note: [Col. 0138D] The manuscript of the cathedral church adds:], [and [Col. 0138D] the offering mentioned above shall be divided among the two canons].

Then, while the magi are praying and as though overcome by sleep, a certain boy dressed in a white garment, with an amice over his head like an angel, shall say this antiphon to them from the pulpit [al. “before the altar”]: [Note: [Col. 0138] Double-click on the ornament icon that follows to view in full the musical notation whose contents are keyed below.]

^210 “Everything that was prophetically foretold has been fulfilled. Go away, returning by another road, lest you become informers of so great a king and be punished.”

[Col. 0139A] When this has been completed, the kings shall withdraw through the aisle of the church to the area before the fonts, and enter the choir through the left-hand door. The procession shall enter the choir, as is customary on Sundays, with the cantor beginning this responsory: [Note: [Col. 0139] Double-click on the ornament icon that follows to view in full the musical notation whose contents are keyed below.]

“if it should be necessary.”

“Three are the gifts.” Verse: “Of salvation.”

[Col. 0140A] At Mass, the three kings shall govern the choir; they shall sing the Kyrie “Fount of goodness,” the Alleluia, the Sanctus, and the Agnus. Introit: “Behold, he has arrived.” Epistle: “Rise, shine.” The aforementioned servants shall sing the Gradual “All from Sheba.” Verse: “Rise, shine.” Offertory: “The kings of Tarshish.” Then the kings shall make offerings, as shall all who wish, etc.

[Col. 0139]

## OFFICE OF THE SEPULCHRE

(From the manuscript ordinal and book of offices of the Bigot Library.)

[Col. 0139A] ^211 When the third responsory has been completed, the Office of the Sepulchre shall be celebrated as follows. Three deacons [al. adding “canons”] from the principal seat, dressed in dalmatics and having amices over their heads in the likeness of women, carrying little vessels in their hands, shall come through the middle of the choir. Hurrying toward the sepulchre with downcast faces, they shall sing together this verse: [Note: [Col. 0139] Double-click on the ornament icon that follows to view in full the musical notation whose contents are keyed below.]

“Who will roll away the stone for us from the entrance of the tomb?”

When this has been completed, a certain boy, dressed like an angel in a white garment and amice, holding an ear of grain [al. a palm branch] in his hand before the sepulchre, shall say: [Note: [Col. 0139] Double-click on the ornament icon that follows to view in full the musical notation whose contents are keyed below.]

“Whom do you seek in the sepulchre, O worshipers of Christ?”

Mary’s companions shall answer: [Note: [Col. 0139] Double-click on the ornament icon that follows to view in full the musical notation whose contents are keyed below.]

[Col. 0139C] “Jesus of Nazareth, the crucified one, O inhabitants of heaven.”

Then the angel [al. adding “opening the sepulchre”] shall say: [Note: [Col. 0139] Double-click on the ornament icon that follows to view in full the musical notation whose contents are keyed below.]

“He is not here, for he has risen, as he said. ^212 Come and see the place where he had been laid, and go and tell his disciples and Peter that he has risen.” [Col. 0139D]

And, pointing out the place with his finger, when this has been completed [al. “done”], the angel shall depart very quickly [al. adding “the women shall enter the sepulchre, since they did not find him”]. Two priests from the principal seat, sitting inside the sepulchre in tunics, shall say: [Note: [Col. 0139] Double-click on the ornament icon that follows to view in full the musical notation whose contents are keyed below.]

“Woman, why are you weeping?”

The middle one of the three women [al. adding “in the place of Mary Magdalene”] shall answer, saying: [Note: [Col. 0139] Double-click on the ornament icon that follows to view in full the musical notation whose contents are keyed below.]

“Because they have taken away my Lord, and I do not know where they have laid him.”

[Col. 0140A] The two sitting inside shall say: [Note: [Col. 0140] Double-click on the ornament icon that follows to view in full the musical notation whose contents are keyed below.]

[Col. 0140B] “Whom do you seek—the living among the dead? He is not here, but has risen. Remember how he spoke to you while he was still in ^213 Galilee, saying: It is necessary for the Son of Man to suffer and [Col. 0140C] be crucified, and on the third day to rise again.”

The women shall kiss the place, and afterward leave the sepulchre. Meanwhile, a priest [al. adding “canon”] from the principal seat, dressed in white as the person of the Lord, with a stole and holding a cross, meeting them at the left corner of the altar, shall say: [Note: [Col. 0140] Double-click on the ornament icon that follows to view in full the musical notation whose contents are keyed below.]

“Woman, why are you weeping? Whom are you seeking?”

The middle one of the women shall say: [Note: [Col. 0140] Double-click on the ornament icon that follows to view in full the musical notation whose contents are keyed below.]

“Lord, if you have taken him away, tell me, and I will take him.”

[Col. 0140D] The priest, showing her the cross, shall say: [Note: [Col. 0140] Double-click on the ornament icon that follows to view in full the musical notation whose contents are keyed below.]

“Mary.”

When she hears this, she shall immediately throw herself at his feet and say in a loud voice: [Note: [Col. 0140] Double-click on the ornament icon that follows to view in full the musical notation whose contents are keyed below.]

“Rabboni.”

The priest, indicating with his hand [al. “drawing back behind him”], shall say: [Note: [Col. 0140] Double-click on the ornament icon that follows to view in full the musical notation whose contents are keyed below.]

^214 “Do not touch me, for I have not yet ascended to my Father; but go to my brothers [Col. 0141A] and tell them: I am ascending to my Father and your Father, my God and your God.”

When this has been completed, the priest shall appear again at the right corner of the altar and say to them as they pass before the altar: [Note: [Col. 0141] Double-click on the ornament icon that follows to view in full the musical notation whose contents are keyed below.]

“Greetings. Do not be afraid. Go, announce to my brothers that they should go [Col. 0141B] to Galilee; there they will see me.”

[Col. 0142A] When this has been completed, he shall hide himself. Having heard this, the women, rejoicing, shall bow toward the altar, then turn toward the choir and sing this verse [al. adding “in a loud voice”]: [Note: [Col. 0142] Double-click on the ornament icon that follows to view in full the musical notation whose contents are keyed below.]

“Alleluia. The Lord has risen; the strong Lion, Christ, the Son of God, has risen.”^215

When this has been completed, the archbishop, or the priest, before the altar with a censer, shall begin loudly “We praise you, O God,” and it shall be concluded without a neume. (At Lauds) the three Marys: “With the Risen One,” or another “Let us bless,” at pleasure. A procession shall follow before the crucifix with the cross throughout the entire week; one of the Marys shall begin “Christ rising,” and the three Marys shall sing the verse at the pulpit, “Let them say now,” etc.

[Col. 0141]

## ORDINATION OF A BISHOP

(From the most ancient manuscript Pontifical of the library of the cathedral of Rouen.)

[Col. 0141B] On the day of the bishop’s ordination, Prime shall be rung and sung very early; afterward they shall go to the chapter house, where the dean, archdeacon, cantor, and chancellor shall appoint those who are to proceed as ministers, as is customary on the greater feasts: namely, two acolytes [Col. 0141C] with censers; two subdeacons with crosses; seven acolytes with candlesticks and candles; seven subdeacons with books of the Gospels; seven deacons with holy relics; twelve priests dressed in chasubles; and an acolyte dressed in a podere with a golden vessel of chrism.

Terce shall be rung at the appointed time. Meanwhile, the lord archbishop shall prepare himself with sandals and ^216 everything else up to the dalmatic. Then he shall put on a cope and, holding the pastoral staff in his hand, shall proceed from the sacristy. Likewise all the bishops shall come out dressed.

The elected man, however, shall not yet put on sandals, but only an alb, stole, and cope; nor shall he carry a staff. Instead, the staff shall be placed upon the altar, together with the ring, until, once consecrated, he receives them from the hand of the archbishop.

When they come into the church, the seats shall be arranged as follows: The metropolitan lord shall sit with his back turned toward the altar; the seats of the other bishops shall be placed before the metropolitan’s eyes. The seat of the elected man shall be placed in the middle, though not at the high altar.

The bishops of the ecclesiastical province shall present the elected man to the metropolitan lord with these words:

“Reverend Father, holy Mother Church N. requests that you raise this priest, who is present, to the burden of the episcopate.”

The metropolitan shall answer:

“Do you know that he is worthy?”

The bishops:

“We know and believe that he is worthy, insofar as human frailty permits us to know.”

And all shall answer:

“Thanks be to God.”

Then the metropolitan shall say to the bishops:

“Let us hear, if it please you, what the holy Fathers decreed concerning so great a consecration.”

Then the chancellor shall read these decrees distinctly and clearly for understanding, saying:

“Command, lord, that I bless.”

And the lord shall say:

“Whatever is displeasing to Christ in us, may the Holy Spirit cleanse.”

^217 From the Decrees of Pope Anacletus. Anacletus, bishop, to all the bishops established in Italy.

Then the metropolitan shall say to the elected man:

“You have heard, dearest, what the ancient institution of the holy Fathers teaches and commands: that the man who is chosen for the order of the episcopate [Col. 0142B] should be examined beforehand with the utmost diligence and complete charity concerning the faith of the Holy Trinity, as we read especially in the Carthaginian canon; and that he should be questioned about the various matters and conduct appropriate to this government, and about what must be retained according to the Apostle’s saying: ‘Lay hands hastily on no one’ (1 Tim. 5:22).

“And also, the man who is to be ordained must first be instructed concerning how one placed under this government ought to conduct himself in the Church of God, so that those who impose upon him the hands of ordination may be irreproachable.

“By the same divine authority and command, we ask you, dearest brother, with sincere charity, whether you are willing, insofar as your nature is capable, to conform all your understanding to the meanings of divine Scripture?” [Note: [Col. 0141] In the Roman Ordo and Pontifical the response reads: “Thus, with all my heart, I am willing to obey and consent in all things.”]

Interrogation. “Are you willing to teach, both by words and by example, the people over whom you are to be ordained, those things which you have understood from the divine Scriptures?”

Response. “I am willing.”

Interrogation. “By the grace of God and your diligence, are you willing to be such as the Apostle teaches a bishop ought to be: namely, sober, prudent, chaste, well adorned, hospitable, a teacher, not given to wine, not violent, but moderate, not quarrelsome, not greedy?” (1 Tim. 3).

Response. “I am willing.”

[Col. 0142D] Interrogation. “Are you willing, God granting it, to preserve purity of mind and body, and to nurture your sons in it?”

Response. “I am willing.”

Interrogation. “Are you willing to be subject to blessed Peter and to the holy Roman Church according to the statutes of the Fathers?”

Response. “I am willing.”

Interrogation. “Are you willing to be obedient and subject to the holy Church of Rouen, and to me and my successors?”

Response. “I am willing.”

Interrogation. “Are you willing to make a profession to me and to my Church, as the custom established from ancient times has required?”

Response. “I am willing, and I am prepared to obey in all things.”

Interrogation. “Are you willing, for the sake of the Lord’s name, to be approachable and merciful toward the poor and pilgrims and all those in need?”

Response. “I am willing.”

Then this prayer shall be said to him:

“May the Lord grant you all these things and every other good thing, [Col. 0143A] and preserve and strengthen you in all goodness.”

And all shall answer:

“Amen.”

Interrogation concerning belief. “Do you believe, according to the understanding and capacity of your mind, that the Holy Trinity—that is, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit—is naturally and essentially one God, almighty, eternal, and unchangeable; and yet that the Father himself is not the one who is the Son, nor the Son himself the one who is the Father, nor the Holy Spirit himself the one who is the Father or the Son, but that the Father is always Father, the Son always Son, and the Holy Spirit always Holy Spirit?”

Response. “I believe.”

Interrogation. “Do you believe that the Father is fully God in himself, the Son fully God in himself, and the Holy Spirit fully God in himself, and yet that these three persons are not three Gods but one living and true God, from whom all things exist, through whom all things exist, and in whom are all things that are in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible?”

Response. “I assent and so believe.”

[Col. 0143B] Interrogation. “Do you believe our Lord Jesus Christ to be true, complete, and perfect God, co-almighty and in all things co-equal with the Father in divinity; temporally born of the Holy Spirit from Mary ever-Virgin, with a rational soul; possessing two births, one eternal from the Father, the other temporal from his mother; true God and true man, proper and perfect in each nature, ^220 not adopted, not imaginary, one and unique God, the Son of God, in two natures and in the singularity of one person; impassible and immortal in his divinity, but in his humanity suffering for us and for our salvation with a true suffering of the flesh; on the fortieth day after the resurrection ascending into heaven with the flesh in which he rose and with his soul, and sitting at the right hand of the Father; from there coming to judge the living and the dead, and rendering to each according to his works?”

Response. “I believe.”

Interrogation. “Do you believe that the bread placed upon the Lord’s table is bread only before consecration, [Col. 0143C] but that in the consecration itself, by the ineffable power of divinity, the nature and substance of bread are changed into the nature and substance of flesh—and not the flesh of another, but that which was conceived of the Holy Spirit and born of the Virgin Mary?”

Response. “I believe.”

Interrogation. “Likewise, do you believe that the wine mixed with water and offered in the chalice for sacrifice is truly and essentially changed into that blood which flowed from the wound in the Lord’s side, pierced by the soldier’s spear?”

Response. “I believe.”

Interrogation. “Do you believe in one holy, catholic, and apostolic Church, in which this singular grace is effected, in which one baptism is given, and true remission of all sins?”

Response. “I believe.”

Interrogation. “Do you anathematize every heresy that exalts itself against this holy catholic Church?”

Response. “I anathematize it.”

Interrogation. “Do you believe in the true resurrection of the same flesh that you now bear, and in eternal life?” [Col. 0143D]

Response. “I believe.”

Prayer.

“May this faith be increased in you by the Lord for true and eternal salvation [al. blessedness], dearest brother.”

Prayer at Mass.

“Be present, O Lord, at our supplications, and may what must be done through the ministry of our humility be accomplished by the effect of your power. Through …”

Another.

“Be gracious, O Lord, to our supplications, and, having inclined over this servant of yours the horn of priestly grace, pour out upon him the power of your blessing. Through …”

Secret.

“May this offering, we ask, O Lord, cleanse our offenses, and sanctify the bodies and minds of those subject to you for the celebration of the sacrifice. Through …”

Infra-action.

^222 “Therefore, this offering of our service, and also of your entire household, which we offer to you even for your servant N., whom you have deigned to promote to the order of the episcopate, we ask, O Lord, that you graciously accept, and mercifully preserve your gifts in him, so that what he has attained by divine favor he may attain through divine effects, and our days …”

Postcommunion.

“May this communion cleanse us from guilt and make us sharers in heavenly [Col. 0144B] healing. Through …”

For consecrating the thumb.

“God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who willed to raise you to pontifical dignity, may he himself pour over you chrism and the liquid of mystical anointing, and make you fruitful with the abundance of spiritual blessing, so that whatever you sanctify may be sanctified, and the laying on of this consecrated hand or thumb may benefit all for salvation. Through …”

Blessing of the staff.

“Almighty and merciful God, who in ineffable goodness assist the vows of those who beseech you, and who, from the abundance of your mercy, grant the desire to ask, pour abundantly the power of your blessing upon this staff, which we dedicate in your name as a sign of pastoral office, so that the shepherd marked with it may carefully guard your people, in such a way that he permits them in no respect to deviate from the unity of the Church, but restores what is unbroken, strengthens what is shattered, and preserves himself together with his flock whole and undefiled for you. Through …”

Blessing of the ring.

“God, beginning and end of all creation, in whom all things are enclosed, deign to bless and sanctify this ring, so that, through it, you who grant your servant the insignia of honor may also bestow virtue and rewards, whereby he may always retain the habit of discernment and shine with the radiance of true faith; and, armed with the protection of the Holy Trinity, may he, as an unconquerable soldier, constantly overcome the battle-line of the devil. Through …”

Here the bishop is placed in the episcopal chair, and this prayer is said:

“Almighty and eternal God, who have deigned to arrange all the heavenly host in distinct orders in the seats above, and who exalted the blessed apostle Peter to the chair of honor of the whole Church, and willed that Matthias, his companion, should sit upon the apostolic throne, we ask, in your immense mercy, ^224 pour out your grace in this place, so that this seat may be a chair of honor and dignity in the sight of your majesty, for the praise and glory of your name and for the honor of your Church; so that whoever sits in it by your choosing may have the sevenfold grace of your Spirit rest upon him. Through our Redeemer, the Lord Jesus Christ, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the same Holy Spirit, God. Through …”

[Col. 0145]

## NAMES OF THOSE TO BE EXCOMMUNICATED

(From the same manuscript Pontifical.)

[Col. 0145A] These are the persons to be summoned: William of Arcis, son of Hubert; Roger Arundel; William of Vernum.

These are the persons to be excommunicated: Robert, son of Helgo; William of Poilley; Gunfrid of Falaise; Walter, deacon of Saint-Leodegar; Herbert [Col. 0146A] of Tot likewise; Geoffrey of Comanville; Helton’s daughter; Ansgold’s daughter; Richard of the Fountain; Benzelin’s daughter; Ralph of Argento; of Ansgold’s daughters, one of whom Richard has and the other Gislebert. Monks possessing money.

[Col. 0145]

## THE BISHOP’S ADMONITION TO THOSE TO BE ORDAINED

(From the manuscript Pontifical of the library of the cathedral of Rouen.)

[Col. 0145B] ^225 At the celebration of the orders, those to be ordained shall be forewarned that they have made a pure confession of their sins, and those who wish to be in the priestly order shall prepare themselves for Communion. All shall also provide themselves with the necessary vestments and shall have suitable tonsures.

When the orders are conferred, a sermon may be given, if desired. Afterward, if the orders are general and the bishop wishes, the following prohibitions shall be made, as a warning to those who intrude improperly, in this form:

“By authority of almighty God the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, and under penalty of major excommunication, we prohibit anyone bound by the impediments written below from presenting himself to receive orders contrary to the decrees of the holy Fathers.

“Therefore, first, second, and third, we warn and prohibit, under penalty of anathema, that anyone present himself for ordination unless his person has first been examined, he has been enrolled with a title, and has been written below and summoned. Nor may anyone conscious of mortal sin, or excommunicated or suspended, receive orders unless he first confesses to one possessing authority and is duly absolved.

“Lest ignorance itself remain unknown, we have decided to specify, serially and in order, the irregular persons who, according to the sacred canons, are prohibited from orders:

“Anyone who is a murderer; likewise, an incendiary of churches, or a violent breaker into them [ms. ‘broken’]; likewise, an advocate in a capital case, or a notorious perjurer; likewise, an executor of savage tortures in public administrations; likewise, a simoniac who has illicitly obtained any benefice or title, or who has entered religion in such a manner; likewise, an inventor of or supporter of simoniacal agreements; likewise, an apostate from the faith or from religion who has not been reconciled; likewise, anyone who knowingly receives any orders from heretical or schismatic bishops who do not possess the grace of the apostolic see; likewise, anyone who has promised, under any pretext, an annual pension or any temporal emolument to the person procuring his presentation or promotion, under a false or fictitious title, or under another agreement made with his presenter to return that title to him after he has been ordained, or otherwise not to disturb him on account of that title; likewise, anyone promoted to any orders by skipping an order; likewise, one previously married, unless he does so in a case permitted by law; likewise, no one who knowingly receives any orders while excommunicated and dares to minister in those received; ^227 likewise, a bigamist or the husband of a corrupted woman; likewise, the violator of consecrated virgins; likewise, no sorcerer, necromancer, or teacher or practitioner of forbidden arts; likewise, anyone suffering from a serious or epileptic illness, lunacy, or another incurable disease, or physically impaired; likewise, an illegitimate person, unless sufficient dispensation has been granted for him; likewise, a born serf, without the knowledge and consent of his lord; likewise, no one from another diocese unless he has letters dimissory and also a sufficient title.

“Likewise, we prohibit anyone from receiving the subdiaconate unless he is eighteen years old, the diaconate unless he is twenty, or the priesthood unless he is twenty-three and has completed his twenty-fifth year; likewise, no religious who has not been professed either in law or in fact; likewise, a beneficed parish priest who has not been ordained priest within a year from the time he assumed the cure and obtained peaceful possession, unless by dispensation, which he has also properly used, according to the constitution *Cum exc.*; likewise, no one without a true title, or whose title has been reduced to a non-title, unless by special grace.

“With all these and each of the aforesaid impediments continuing, we command them, under the penalty of excommunication noted above, to abstain from receiving such orders until dispensation has been granted to them. Let careful provision also be made concerning every mutilation of the limbs of those to be ordained in sacred orders; nor may they be hunchbacked, one-handed, or otherwise physically impaired, in order to avoid scandal to the clergy and the Church.

^228 “Because the matter you are about to undertake is sufficiently dangerous, dearest brothers, I admonish you to learn diligently and properly the entire order of the Mass, its consecration, fraction, and communion from other priests already instructed, before you presume to sing your own Mass.”

[Col. 0145]

## BLESSING OF THE ABBOT OF MONKS

(From the same manuscript Pontifical.)

[Col. 0145D] At the ordination and blessing of an abbot by election of the monks, he first comes to the altar dressed in pontifical vestments for the Mass to be said, and says the *Confiteor*, etc. Then he must sit before the altar in his prepared seat. At that point two abbots lead the new abbot before the bishop, dressed in amice, alb, maniple, [Col. 0147A] stole, and cope in place of a chasuble; the assisting abbots are dressed in the same way. Before Mass begins, these assistants shall say:

“The elected man is present,” etc.

The assisting abbots, holding staffs in their hands, shall sit in order on a bench at the step of the altar. The elected man, however, shall not carry a staff; it shall be placed upon the altar until he receives it from the hand of the bishop. After the pontiff has said the *Confiteor*, etc., and before the Introit of the Mass begins, the assisting abbots shall say:

^229 “Reverend Father, our elected man is present to receive his blessing.”

Question to be put by the bishop: “Do you know that this elected brother is suitable for the office of abbot?”

Response: “We know, insofar as human frailty permits us to know.”

Question: “Has he been elected by the brothers according to the rule of blessed Benedict?”

Response: “The canonical election of the brothers has agreed upon him.”

Question by the bishop: “Do you have the written document concerning this?”

Response: [Col. 0147B] “We have it.”

The bishop: “Let it be read.”

Then the document or proceedings shall be read. If, however, he has been elected by apostolic provision, the assisting abbots, presenting the elected man for blessing, shall say:

“Reverend Father, our elected man is present to receive his blessing.”

Question by the bishop: “Has he been canonically elected?”

The abbots: “The canonical election has agreed upon him by apostolic provision.”

^230 The bishop: “Do you have the written document concerning this?”

The abbots: “We have it.”

The bishop: “Let it be read.”

Then let the document of provision be read. When it has been read, the bishop shall say:

“Since, therefore, the votes of the brothers agree in his favor, we first judge that he must be examined by apostolic authority, to determine whether he himself wishes to observe his purpose and the Rule of Saint Benedict, diligently instruct those subject to him to do the same, and, insofar as he is able, gather together the goods of his establishments that have hitherto been unjustly dispersed, distributing them for the use of the Church, the brothers, the poor, and pilgrims; and thus whether he is worthy to approach ordination. Therefore we ask you, brother: do you wish to live according to the rule of Saint N. or Benedict, and regularly instruct those subject to you to do the same?”

Response: “I do.”

Question by the bishop: “Do you wish faithfully to guard the goods and possessions of the Church entrusted to you, gathered together there, and, insofar as you are able, recover those unjustly dispersed, distributing them faithfully for the use of the Church, the brothers, the poor, and pilgrims?”

Response: “I do.”

Question by the bishop: “Do you wish to be benevolent and hospitable toward the poor and pilgrims?”

Response: “I do.”

Question by the bishop: “Do you wish to adorn your order with religious habit and holy conduct?”

Response: “I do.”

Question by the bishop: “Do you wish to show subjection and obedience to the holy Church of N., to me, and to my successors, according to canonical authority and the decrees of the holy pontiffs?”

[Note: Concerning the subjection and obedience of abbots to their bishops, see Saint Bernard, *De consideratione*, book III, chapter 3, and the treatise *De officio episcoporum*, chapter 9.]

Response: “I do.”

The bishop: “May God increase your faith and steadfastness, so that you may be able to keep your promises and faithfully fulfill them.”

The clergy shall respond: “Amen.”

After this has been said, the bishop shall begin the antiphon, with the choir continuing it.

Antiphon: “Confirm, O God, what you have wrought in us, from your holy temple which is in Jerusalem, alleluia, alleluia.”

Psalm: “Let God arise.” The entire psalm is said with “Glory be to the Father” and “As it was,” beginning the antiphon “Confirm” again.

If a Mass other than that for an abbot is celebrated, after the collect of the day the following prayer is said under one conclusion, “Through the Lord.”

[Col. 0148A]

## At Mass

Introit. Office.

“Our protector, look upon us, O God.” Psalm: “How lovely are your tabernacles, O Lord,” etc.

Let us pray. Prayer.

“Grant, we ask, O Lord, to [another reading adds: ‘this’] your elect servant N., that by preaching and practicing what is right, he may instruct the minds of his subjects by the example of good works, and may receive from you, most merciful Shepherd, the reward of eternal recompense. Through [the Lord].”

When the prayer has ended, the bishop and the elect, together with the assisting abbots, shall prostrate themselves before the altar. The seven penitential psalms shall be said, and the litanies shall be sung.

When “That [you would …] our pontiff” has been said, the bishop alone shall rise and say:

“That you would deign to bless [bene+dicere] this elect man, we ask you.”

The choir shall respond: “That you would deign to bless [bene+dicere] this elect man,” etc.

The bishop: “That you would deign to bless [bene+dicere] and sanctify [sancti+ficare] this elect man, we ask you.”

“That you would deign to bless [bene+dicere], sanctify [sancti+ficare], and consecrate [conse+crare] this elect man, we ask you.”

After this has been said, the bishop shall prostrate himself again, and the litany shall be completed. When it has been said, the bishop shall say silently:

“Our Father,” and, in the manner of prayers, “And lead us not into temptation.”

The choir: “But deliver us from evil.”

Afterward:

The bishop: “Save your servant.”

The choir: “My God.”

The bishop: “May the Lord guard your going in and your coming out.”

The choir: “From this time forth.”

The bishop: “May the Lord guard you from every evil.”

The choir: “May the Lord guard your soul.”

The bishop: “May the enemy accomplish nothing against him.”

The choir: “And may the son of iniquity do him no harm.”

The bishop: “Be for him, O Lord, a tower of strength.”

The choir: “Against the face of the enemy.”

The bishop: “Arise, O Lord; help us.”

The choir: “And deliver us.”

The bishop: “Lord, God of hosts, convert us.”

The choir: “And show us.”

The bishop: “O Lord, hear us.”

The choir: “And our cry.”

The bishop: “The Lord be with you.”

The choir: “And with your spirit.”

The following prayers are said in the manner of a prayer.

[Col. 0148C]

### Prayer

“Grant, we ask, almighty God, that the desire of our humility may obtain the effect of your mercy, and accompany with the gift of your grace this servant of yours whom we elect to govern souls, so that, by your generosity, we may please you through this election of ours. Through Christ.”

Let us pray.

“Lord God almighty, hear our prayers, and send upon this servant of yours the spirit of your blessing, so that, enriched with a heavenly gift, he may be able to obtain the grace of your majesty and offer others an example of good living. Through [the Lord].”

Let us pray.

“Hear, O Lord, our prayers, which we pour out in the presence of your majesty over this servant of yours, who is appointed in place of your name to govern your sheep. May you deign to look upon him and, through the intervention of blessed Benedict, our patron and governor, to bless him. You who descended from heaven for our redemption and protection, and showed yourself to the world as God and the supreme [or: supreme and true] Shepherd, saying, ‘I am the good shepherd’ (John XI, 14), we invoke you and humbly beseech you: may your goodness be with this servant of yours, whom you have willed to undertake the summit of pastoral office, and may your blessing be with him all the days of his life.

“Protect him, O Lord, and defend him from every adversity of visible and invisible enemies. Direct his steps in the way of peace and justice, and bestow upon him the gifts of your virtues: justice, temperance [with the addition in another version: prudence, charity, sobriety, patience], strength and long-suffering, unconquerable steadfastness, unfeigned faith, unshaken hope, devoted mind, perfect humility, sound understanding, kindness, modesty, unanimity, peace, concord, chastity, abstinence, vigilance, discernment, uprightness, knowledge, piety, counsel, and inviolable perseverance in every good action.

“Take away from him, Lord Jesus Christ, whatever is wicked and distorted, and [another reading: ‘is’] whatever is contrary to salvation, whatever is harmful to the soul [another reading: injurious], pride, boasting, empty glory, arrogance, and whatever in the end may be displeasing. Surround him within and without with the aid of your protection, so that, with you as his defender, he may be safe; with you protecting him, secure; with you teaching him, knowledgeable.

“Show him the way on which he should walk. Grant him the treasures of wisdom, so that he may know and possess the means to bring forth things new and old. Make him follow your footsteps in all things and obtain good joy from his ministry, so that, after the course of this age, when he has come before your tribunal, you may also grant, with the multiplied fruit of souls, to him [another reading adds: ‘to him’] and to all those whom he will present to you that reward which you promised [another reading: promised beforehand] to give in heaven to your faithful stewards who labor on earth in your name, You who, with God the Father, etc. Amen.”

Then the bishop shall hand him the rule, reading it and saying:

“Receive the rule handed down to us by the holy Fathers, for governing and guarding the flock entrusted to you by God, insofar as God himself has appointed for you and human frailty has permitted.”

Afterward he shall give him the staff, reading and saying:

“Receive the staff of pastoral office, which you are to bear before the company entrusted to you, as an example of just severity and correction.”
